# Types

**Audience:** Edva users<br>
**Status:** current reference<br>
**Audited:** `8b8cb19`<br>
**Evidence:** `src/types.dva`, `src/annotate.dva`, `tests/pass/`

Edva is statically typed. It never defaults an unknown type to `Int`; a value
must be typed by an annotation, a function signature, a literal suffix, or
unification with surrounding expressions. Function values carry only a
function pointer and environment pointer—there is no runtime type descriptor,
RTTI, vtable, or dynamic function signature.

## Recognized names

The primitive names are `Int`, `Float`, `String`, `Rune`, `Builder`, `Addr`,
and `Error`, plus LLVM-width scalar types. `Type` is a compile-time-only value
representing a type; it cannot be lowered at runtime. Other type names must be
declared with `#type`.

```dva
#type Point (x: Int, y: Int)       // named record with two Int fields
#type Points (Point){}             // growable array whose elements are Point
#type ByName String ^ Point         // map from String keys to Point values
#type Colour < Red, Green, Blue >   // enum with three named unit variants

// The four ram layouts:
flag: <>                            // RamNN: the built-in flag, both slots unit
#type MaybePoint < Point | >        // RamPN: Point payload or negative unit
#type Failed < | Error >             // RamNP: positive unit or Error payload
#type Result < Point | Error >       // RamPP: Point payload or Error payload
```

Records may have named or positional fields. `(T){}` is a growable array,
`K ^ V` a map, `<...>` a ramification, and an enum uses named variants in its
angle-bracket declaration. The `<>` flag is a built-in type, so it needs no
`#type` declaration. Records and array-like values retain structural shape;
all four ramification layouts are incompatible static types.

## Unit

`()` is the Unit **type**. It is valid only in a declaration—for example, as
the result type in a function signature or as a component of a composite type.
It is not a runtime literal to write as an expression.

Unit is the result of an assignment and of a statement choice. It is also what
a ram produces when the selected slot is a unit slot: both slots of `<>`, the
second slot of `< T | >`, and the first slot of `< | E >`. A function returns
the value of its last expression, so a function whose final expression is an
assignment or an inexhaustive statement choice returns Unit.

## Composite types

Composite types describe values made from other values. They are structural:
the shape of fields, elements, slots, or parameters matters to type checking.
Use `#type` to give a composite shape a reusable name.

### Records and homogeneous records

A record has named fields or positional fields. A homogeneous record repeats a
single element type and uses a fixed `* count` form.

```dva
#type Point (x: Int, y: Int)       // record with named fields
#type Pair (Int, String)            // record with positional fields
#type Bytes (i8 * 16)               // 16-element homogeneous record
```

Read named fields with `.name` and positional fields with `.0`, `.1`, and so
on. A record declared only with a forward annotation is not zero-initialized:
every field must be definitely initialized before a read. A homogeneous record
must receive a whole-value initialization before any element read or write.

### Growable arrays and slices

A growable array type has the form `(T){}`. It owns resizable element storage;
`?array` returns its element count and `++array` makes a copy. Indexing is
fallible and returns a ramification, so `array(index)!!` is the concise
unwrap-or-panic form.

```dva
#type Ints (Int){}                 // growable array of Int
values = Ints()
values += 42
```

Slices are non-owning views of homogeneous storage. Their element count is
also measured with `?`; unlike growable arrays, their lifetime is bounded by
the storage that they view.

### Maps

A map type is `Key ^ Value`. Its key type is `String`, `Int`, or `Addr`; its
value type may be any storable shape. Empty maps use a named type, while a
non-empty literal can infer its map type from key/value pairs.

```dva
#type Scores String ^ Int           // map from String to Int
scores = Scores()
scores ^ "Ada" = 5
```

Map lookup returns `< Value | Error >`, membership returns a flag, and
`?map` reports its entry count. See [data and memory](../../guide/data-and-memory.qmd)
for operations, initialization, and failure handling.

### Rams and enums

A ramification has exactly two positional slots. It models flag, optional, and
fallible values; the four layouts are shown above. An enum has two or more
named variants, each optionally carrying payload fields.

```dva
#type Token < Identifier(String), Number(Int), End >
#type ParseResult < Token | Error >
```

Match an enum with adjacent `[Variant]` or `[Variant payload]` branches. Match
a ram only with positional bare branches; ram slots have no names. The
[ramifications guide](../../guide/ramifications.qmd) explains constructors and
matching in detail.

### Function and recursive types

A function type lists its parameter types and return type. When a function
type occurs inside another type or signature, wrap it in parentheses.

```dva
#type Handler (run: (Int => Int))   // record carrying a function value
#type Tree < Leaf(Int), Branch((Tree[])) >
```

Type names are registered before their definitions finish parsing. That makes
recursive and mutually recursive records, rams, and enums possible; a type
name that is never declared remains an unknown-type diagnostic.

## Initialization and conversion

A forward-annotated record is not zero-filled. Each field must be written on
every path before it is read, and a partially initialized composite cannot be
passed to another function. Homogeneous records need whole-value
initialization before element access.

Conversions are explicit. Use `Int(value)`, `Rune(value)`, and the relevant
width type where a conversion is supported. There is no implicit integer/float
conversion, no flag/heap-ram conversion, and no conversion from one ram shape
to another. The sole ram cast, `<>(ram)`, discards payload and returns a flag.

Read [ramifications](../../guide/ramifications.qmd) for ram shapes and
[data and memory](../../guide/data-and-memory.qmd) for container behavior.
